llm_narrative: Across the 500 evaluation tasks, granite4.1_3b_output achieved a mean claim‑coverage of only 0.0509 (median 0), indicating that virtually none of the required statements were satisfied. The failure analysis shows that 68.1 % (339) of the errors stemmed from pure cognitive breakdowns while 31.9 % (159) involved tool‑call problems, yet the most common symptom was early termination – 205 instances where the model stopped before producing a final answer despite having completed the necessary calls. Wrong‑tool selection (92 cases), task misunderstanding (93 cases), and outright omission of any tool use (45 cases) together account for roughly one‑third of all failures, reflecting a systematic difficulty in mapping multi‑step prompts to the appropriate MCP interfaces. A concrete remediation is to augment the fine‑tuning data with explicit “must‑answer” scaffolding and end‑of‑conversation checks that force the model to synthesize and emit a final response after the last tool result is received. What sets this model apart from other evaluated systems is the disproportionate number of empty or prematurely ended replies (229 empty responses) – the model frequently gathers correct evidence but never translates it into output, revealing a bottleneck at the synthesis stage rather than at information retrieval.
